dialogue: 女主："为什么……骗我的是你……为什么？为什么！"
prompt:
shot from the male lead's first-person position, standing directly in front of her on the snowfield at her eye level, the same spot for the whole take. locked-off camera, the axis stays fixed for the whole take and she keeps looking straight into the lens. one medium close-up held for the whole take. the same young woman throughout, same face, same long black hair, same red scarf over black robes.

Medium close-up on her upper body, her sword hand, and the blade angled up toward the lens; she keeps the sword where it already is, tip aimed at the lens, and her grip closes harder on the hilt until the blade tip picks up a fine, real tremor. Her brow draws in a fraction at a time, her eyelids lower, her jaw sets, her back teeth clamp, and her nostrils flare with shallow, held-in breaths. Driven snow streams in from screen left through her long hair, the loose strands at her forehead, her red scarf and her hem; snow grains settle on the ends of her hair and on her lashes, and her breath leaves a faint white plume. She speaks in Mandarin Chinese, low and forced out between her teeth, breaking off with a heavy breath before the volume climbs into a demand, the feeling stepping up while she holds it in: "为什么……骗我的是你……为什么？为什么！". Howling wind and driven snow, her breathing.

dialogue: 女主："今天……我们……只能活一个。"
prompt:
shot from the male lead's first-person position, standing directly in front of her on the snowfield at her eye level, the same spot for the whole take. locked-off camera on the same fixed axis, and her eyes stay locked on the lens. medium close-up, widening slightly to take in the whole sword arm and blade, held until the blade tip fills the frame. the same young woman throughout, same face, same long black hair, same red scarf over black robes.

First, medium close-up, her face and the raised blade both in frame; her gaze is already settled and steady on the lens; as the last word leaves her, her lips press shut, her jaw holds, and her breathing steadies. She speaks in Mandarin Chinese, pitched as low and as heavy as she can, squeezing out a fact she would rather leave unsaid, every syllable stressed, quieter than a shout and flatter than a declaration: "今天……我们……只能活一个。". Howling wind and driven snow.

Then, the framing widens a little to take in her sword hand, elbow, shoulder and the full length of the blade; the full wind-up plays out with every stage of it visible: her fingers clamp onto the hilt, her wrist lifts the hilt a short way straight up, then her sword hand and the whole blade travel back along one clear arc, her elbow pulls back, her shoulder closes in with it, her upper body twists and presses toward the far side, the load builds to full, and there is a very brief dead hold at the top of it. Her eyes stay on the lens the whole time while wind lifts her long hair and red scarf hard. Wind tearing at cloth, the rush of the blade loading.

Finally, the same framing, holding until the blade tip fills the frame; she releases all of it at once and drives the sword straight into the lens, short, fast, hard and clean, with the tip rushing from dead centre of frame right up to the lens until it covers the whole frame; her eyes stay locked on the lens, and the image freezes on the single instant the tip reaches the lens and turns to high-contrast black and white. The blade tearing the air, rising sharply, then cutting to silence on the freeze.
